whatChanged.categoryZh: AI / 教育 / 产品政策
whatChanged.headline: Schools Can Switch Off Google's AI. Why Does Search Go Off Too?
whatChanged.headlineZh: 学校可以关闭 Google AI，为什么连搜索也要一起关？
intro: Google says it will disable Gemini and related AI features by default for K–12 student accounts until school administrators choose to enable them. But there is a catch: a school that does not allow Google's AI-powered features cannot keep ordinary Google Search switched on for those accounts either.
The announcement on 3 November 2026 turns a familiar classroom debate into a practical product question: how much choice do schools really have when AI is built into search?
introZh: Google 2026 年 11 月 3 日宣布，将默认关闭中小学学生账号里的 Gemini 等 AI 功能，是否启用由学校管理员决定。可问题是：如果学校不接受 Google 搜索中的 AI 功能，就不能只保留传统的 Google Search。
学校想控制学生怎么使用 AI，却发现搜索和 AI 已经被绑在一起。这次调整究竟给了学校多少选择权？

sections.heading: What exactly changes for student accounts?
sections.headingZh: 学生账号具体会发生什么变化？
paragraphs: According to reporting by the Associated Press and The Guardian on 3 November, Google is moving to an opt-in approach for AI features on K–12 school accounts. Administrators, rather than individual students, decide whether to enable them. The affected products include Gemini and AI features integrated into Google Search. This is about managed school accounts, not a claim that Google Search is being switched off for everyone.

Google presents the change as a way to give schools control after concerns about children's use of AI. Its new Guided Learning approach is designed to walk students through a problem rather than simply provide an answer. That educational design, however, does not resolve the separate issue of whether schools can choose search without generative AI.
paragraphsZh: 据美联社和《卫报》2026 年 11 月 3 日报道，Google 将中小学学生账号的 AI 功能改为默认关闭，由学校管理员决定是否开启，涉及 Gemini 及整合进 Google Search 的 AI 功能。这里说的是学校管理的学生账号，不是所有人的 Google 搜索都会被关闭。
Google 的解释是，这样可以回应家长和教育工作者对学生使用 AI 的担忧。它还推出 Guided Learning，希望 AI 遇到学习题目时引导学生一步步思考，而不是直接给答案。但这和学校能否单独关闭搜索里的 AI，是两回事。

sections.heading: Why can't schools simply turn off AI in Search?
sections.headingZh: 为什么不能只保留传统搜索？
paragraphs: Google says AI has become integral to its search product. AI Overviews and conversational search are no longer treated as an entirely separate service that an administrator can always disable while retaining the rest of Search. Under the announced arrangement, refusing those AI features also means losing Google Search access for the relevant school accounts.

That matters because searching the web and asking a chatbot to generate an answer are not identical learning activities. Teachers may want students to compare sources, check claims and read original pages while restricting generated responses. A single combined switch makes that distinction harder to enforce through Google's own settings.
paragraphsZh: Google 认为 AI 已经成为搜索产品的一部分。AI Overviews 等功能与搜索深度整合，学校不能简单地在自己的管理设置里关闭所有生成式 AI，同时继续使用同一套 Google Search。
可对老师来说，“让学生自己查资料”和“让 AI 直接生成答案”并不是同一种学习方式。老师可能希望学生比较不同网页、追查来源，却暂时不使用生成式回答。把两者放在同一个开关里，学校就很难按照自己的教学方式做区分。

sections.heading: Who objects, and what remains uncertain?
paragraphs: Critics cited by AP, including the child-advocacy organisation Fairplay and former US Federal Trade Commission chair Lina Khan, argue that tying search access to AI choices puts pressure on schools. Google says the approach gives school administrators control over whether to enable the affected products.

The precise implementation schedule and options may vary by product and school configuration. This report does not establish that all schools worldwide have already lost search access, or that a school cannot use other search services. The change is a Google account-control decision, not a law requiring AI in classrooms.
paragraphsZh: 美联社引述的儿童权益组织 Fairplay 及美国联邦贸易委员会前主席 Lina Khan 等批评者认为，这种捆绑可能迫使学校在搜索和 AI 之间做不必要的选择。Google 则强调，最终是否启用相关功能仍由学校管理员决定。
需要注意：这不意味着全球所有学校现在都无法搜索，也不意味着学校不能选择其他搜索服务。不同产品及学校配置的具体实施时间和控制选项，仍应以 Google 后续正式说明为准。这是 Google 的产品政策，不是政府强制学校使用 AI 的法律。

whatChanged.ending: For schools, the important question may be less whether AI is useful than whether they can decide where it belongs.
whatChanged.endingZh: 学校要决定的，不只是 AI 有没有用，还有它应该在哪些学习环节出现。

stayCurious.categoryZh: 新加坡 / 历史 / 建筑
stayCurious.headline: Why Is Singapore's Oldest Surviving Fire Station Called “Blood and Bandage”?
stayCurious.headlineZh: 新加坡最古老的现存消防局，为什么叫“血与绷带”？
intro: On Hill Street in Singapore stands a fire station with striking red-and-white walls. The building is nicknamed “Blood and Bandage”. The name sounds dramatic, but it comes from the colours of the building, not a particular emergency.
Completed in 1908, Central Fire Station is still a working station. Its walls tell a story about how a growing city learned to fight fires.
introZh: 新加坡 Hill Street 上有一栋红白相间的老建筑，外号竟然叫“Blood and Bandage”，血与绷带。
名字听起来有点吓人，其实说的是外墙的颜色。这座 1908 年建成的中央消防局至今仍在使用，也是新加坡现存最古老的消防局。

sections.heading: Where did the strange nickname come from?
sections.headingZh: “血与绷带”这个外号从哪儿来？
paragraphs: The National Heritage Board explains that the building's red-and-white brickwork inspired the nickname. Its architecture reflects a style popular in Edwardian England in the early twentieth century. There is a small visual trick: the white sections were not white bricks. They were bricks covered in plaster and painted white.
The distinctive façade makes the station easy to recognise today. It was designated a national monument in 1998, preserving an important part of Singapore's early civic infrastructure.
paragraphsZh: 新加坡国家文物局介绍，这个外号来自建筑红白相间的外墙。它采用了 20 世纪初英国爱德华时代流行的建筑风格。还有个容易看错的细节：白色部分并不是白砖，而是在砖墙外抹灰，再刷上白漆。
1998 年，中央消防局被列为新加坡国家古迹。这栋建筑不只是好看，也保存了城市早期公共安全设施的一段历史。

sections.heading: Was it Singapore's very first fire station?
sections.headingZh: 它是新加坡第一座消防局吗？
paragraphs: No. “Oldest surviving” is different from “first ever”. The Singapore Civil Defence Force's historical publication records that Cross Street Station was built in 1891. The Hill Street station was completed in 1908, during a period when firefighting was becoming more organised and better equipped.

The National Heritage Board's Civic District Heritage Trail describes how Superintendent Montague William Pett, who arrived in 1904, helped modernise the service with motorised fire engines, better communications and more street hydrants. A purpose-built central station was part of that transformation.
paragraphsZh: 不是。“现存最古老”和“历史上第一座”要分开。新加坡民防部队的历史资料记载，Cross Street 早在 1891 年就建有消防局。Hill Street 的中央消防局则于 1908 年建成。
那时，新加坡的消防工作正在现代化。国家文物局的市政区文化遗产步道介绍，1904 年来到新加坡的消防主管 Montague William Pett 推动了机动消防车、通信系统和街道消防栓的发展。新的中央消防局也是这一变化的一部分。

sections.heading: Is it a museum or a working fire station?
sections.headingZh: 现在这里是博物馆，还是消防局？
paragraphs: Both, in different parts of the compound. SCDF identifies Central Fire Station as an operational station serving the city centre. The Civil Defence Heritage Gallery opened within its grounds in November 2001, displaying historic firefighting equipment and the evolution of civil defence. Visitors can learn how the service moved from older firefighting methods to modern rescue work.
The building therefore is not simply a preserved façade. It connects an active emergency service with the city's memory of how that service developed.
paragraphsZh: 两者都是。中央消防局仍然承担市中心的消防救援任务。2001 年 11 月，民防历史展览馆（Civil Defence Heritage Gallery）在消防局内开放，展示老式消防设备、历史文物，以及消防和民防工作如何逐渐演变。
所以这不是一栋只剩外观的老建筑。里面仍有人值勤，也有人来了解一百多年前的新加坡如何应对火灾。

stayCurious.ending: Sometimes a city's history is still on duty.
stayCurious.endingZh: 有些城市历史没有退役，今天还在继续值班。
